A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ECO/SeTR research, renamed from BREASE to HERMES. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable throughout. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v3 includes Appendix A.1–A.7, which was included in the comparison.

before.justification: v1 Tables 1–4 report original LVU classification, MovieChat question-answering results and component ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, efficiency measurements, sensitivity experiments and qualitative successes and failures in the main text and appendix.

M1.justification: The renamed main framework retains the encoder, ECO merging rule, SeTR procedure, Q-Former branches and Vicuna-7B. v3 additionally introduces MA-LMM integration variants that replace its memory bank with ECO or augment it with SeTR (Section 4.3, Table 7). The expanded hierarchical Q-Former description documents an architecture already present in v1 Figure 1 and Section 3.5.

E1.justification: v3 adds actual evaluation on Breakfast and COIN instructional videos, which v1 only cited, substantially extending coverage beyond the original movie benchmarks. It also adds MovieChat-1k breakpoint-mode evaluation alongside retained global-mode QA and LVU classification (Tables 1–3).

E2.justification: v3 removes VidMamba/VideoMamba from the LVU comparison and adds VideoChat to the MovieChat comparison. New comparisons include FACT on Breakfast and ToMe and MA-LMM in compression/latency experiments (Tables 2, 3 and 7; Figure 5). Object Transformer and Movies2Scenes match v1's abbreviated names and are not new comparators.

E3.justification: The retained classification/QA metrics and one-epoch MovieChat training setting remain consistent. New evaluation designs measure latency, sweep 40–1000 input frames while holding episodic capacity and the semantic output count fixed, vary window sizes, and use custom difficult questions for qualitative evaluation (Section 4.4, Appendix A.4). Newly disclosed defaults in Table 8 do not establish revisions to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: The original ECO update and SeTR pooling ablations are retained. v3 adds hierarchical-versus-flat Q-Former ablations, MA-LMM component integration tests, compression-efficiency comparisons, episode/keep-ratio/frame/window sensitivity studies, and qualitative success and failure analyses (Section 4.3, Appendix A.4–A.6). These substantially expand examination of design choices, efficiency and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, dispersion estimates or formal significance tests. The additional v3 tables and plots continue to report point results.

E6.justification: Matched LVU rows, MovieChat global-mode scores and original component ablations retain their values, including 70.3 LVU average accuracy and 78.6% zero-shot global QA accuracy. v3 adds 95.2% on Breakfast, 93.5% on COIN, and breakpoint accuracies of 57.3% zero-shot and 65.8% supervised (Tables 2–3), plus extensive latency, sensitivity and qualitative findings. These are newly reported results, not improvements over v1 under the retained settings.

T1.justification: v3 Section 2 adds a formal problem formulation defining internal understanding U, compressed episodic/semantic mappings and the conditional answering goal P(A|Q,U). This is a limited addition of mathematical definitions, without new proofs or guarantees. The existing ECO merging mathematics is preserved and reformatted as Algorithm 1.

C1.justification: The central cognition-inspired ECO/SeTR contributions and headline LVU/MovieChat gains remain. v3 modestly broadens the explicit state-of-the-art claim from two datasets to four and states that the components can apply to other models (Introduction, Section 3 and Conclusion), without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of hierarchical aggregation, frame redundancy, context-window tradeoffs and component integration. Appendix A.6 identifies contextual, counting and event-inference failures, while A.7 develops the cognitive analogy and explicitly qualifies it as an oversimplified abstraction. These considerably expand v1's limited discussion of component benefits and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1–A.3 and Table 8 add learning rates, batch sizes, frame sampling, episode capacities, keep ratios, epoch limits, checkpoint selection, GPU specifications and runtime information. These substantially improve technical disclosure without establishing changed settings for retained experiments. v1 describes project code as available at its link; v3 describes code as forthcoming and additionally promises pretrained models and processed annotations.

R1.justification: Beyond retaining most video-understanding background, v3 substantially expands cognitive-science positioning in Appendix A.7 through literature on episodic/semantic memory, hippocampal consolidation, event segmentation and gist extraction. It also adds works associated with VideoChat, FACT and sparse-frame motivation, while removing the VideoMamba reference. The related-work section's relocation alone is not counted here.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the narrative: BREASE becomes HERMES, the introduction and contribution list are rewritten, a problem-setting section precedes the framework, and related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5. Method explanations are expanded into dedicated subsections, with organized appendix sections and cross-references replacing the earlier compact presentation.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation. The framework diagram is redrawn and enlarged, the MovieChat table gains grouped global/breakpoint columns, and new conceptual diagrams, component schematics, sensitivity/latency plots and qualitative panels are introduced. Original ablation tables are retained and relocated rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's sparse implementation documentation and limited validation through reproducibility details, instructional-video evaluations, controlled sensitivity studies and explicit failure analysis. These make the retained framework easier to assess and reproduce. Timing definitions remain unclear between Table 7 and Appendix A.4.3, and code-release wording changes from available to forthcoming, but these caveats do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidential support and transparency.
